content:
In the recently merged batteries#1990, doing the mathlib adaptations went very unsmoothly. Firstly, I made some adaptations that I put in a PR (https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4-nightly-testing/pull/306), but nobody merged this PR, causing the breaks-mathlib label to stay. And then later it turned out that my adaptations weren't sufficient, even though CI was green on the adaptation PR.

I would like to make another batteries PR with mathlib adaptations, so I would like to ask, what should I do to prevent these problems in the future?

My understanding is that there are two components to mathlib adaptations. One is a quick fix, so the downstream repositories continue to build. Those need not be carefully reviewed (nor be durable solutions); their point is to enable further testing of more incoming changes, while a proper fix is reviewed.

The second component are the real adaptations to mathlib... which should see proper review. I agree this distinction is not well-documented, and in general perhaps the proper bump processes are unclear. FWIW, there were similar questions on the CSLib side: #ecosystem infrastructure > coordination between downstream-lean4 and downstream-reports

With all that said: I'm not sure myself what the best way forward is here.
@François G. Dorais you modified batteries' documentation about this recently. Can you say something how you envision the process to work?

The only change is that users are now strongly discouraged from PR their own adaptations to mathlib, batteries mods should do this going forward. Users are still expected to PR to the batteries-pr-testing branch as usual. Batteries mods should merge these PRs without much review.
So does that mean that I should do the same as what I did in batteries#1990? How do we make sure the same kind of breakage doesn't happen again?
Your PR to batteries-pr-testing-1990 was merged after batteries#1990 was merged. So batteries#1990 was merged before checking that the adaptation worked. The change is meant to prevent exactly that.

After a more thorough post-mortem, I see that nobody involved did anything fundamentally wrong. The PR had a complicated development history with several people involved. That confused things a bit and resulted in out-of-order steps that only increased general confusion.

@Michael Rothgang: I like your quick-fix/real-fix division; this also reflects a Batteries/Mathlib division. The part that Batteries maintainers need to supervise is the quick-fix part. The real-fix part is really on the Mathlib side.

The revised adaptation process aims to smooth out the quick-fix part. The validity of the quick-fix is now under supervision of Batteries maintainers. (Prior to now, contributors were ultimately fully responsible for their Mathlib adaptations.) This way, nothing is merged in Batteries without a working quick-fix Mathlib adaptation, and all these adaptations are authored by a Batteries maintainer when submitted to Mathlib. (The real-fix should be authored by the contributor or another interested party.)
(To avoid confusion: "validity" just means that it works and doesn't add extra stuff beyond that. It does not mean that Mathlib maintainers should approve without review.)
